This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |

cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. - `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

248	### 4.2 LoRA 控制通道：LoraClient 是能力本身
249	
250	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
251	
252	u3-l5 讲过 `Scheduler` trait 只有三个方法——`submit`、`step`、`metrics`——并且「超出三方法的能力由调度器自建通道、在自己的 step 里排空」。LoRA 适配器的动态装卸就是这句话的实例：装载/卸载适配器会改变引擎的权重状态，必须由调度器在安全时机（批空闲时）应用，因此它不适合塞进 `Scheduler` 契约，而是**一条独立的控制通道**。
253	
254	这条通道的设计核心是一个类型层面的决定：引擎交接包 `Engine` 上挂着 `lora: Option<LoraClient>`。**这个 `Option` 就是能力本身**——`Some` 表示「这个引擎能管理适配器，拿着客户端就能下命令」；`None` 表示「这个引擎没有这门能力」。注意这里**不存在「unsupported」错误路径**：没有铸造通道的引擎压根不会挂载 LoRA 路由，无人能「问」它，也就无需回答。对比一下常见的替代设计（布尔开关 `supports_lora` + 调用时返回 `Unsupported` 错误）：开关与客户端可能不一致（开关开着但客户端忘了给），而 `Option` 里要么有可用的客户端、要么没有，第二种真相源不存在。lora.rs 测试里的一条注释把这一点说得很直白：「An engine without LoRA never mounts these routes at all — the `Option` on `Engine::lora` is the capability」。
255	
256	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
257	
258	```
259	引擎侧（模型 crate，以 qwen3 为例）                    服务侧（frontend）
260	─────────────────────────                            ─────────────────────
261	launch 时：
262	  LoraClient::channel() ──铸出──▶ (client, rx)
263	  rx 交给调度器（spawn 前捕获）
264	  Engine { lora: Some(client), .. } ──────────────▶ serve_model_with_lora_routes
265	                                                      │ 取出 client（None → 显式报错）
266	                                                      ▼
267	调度器每一步：                                    /v1/load_lora_adapter 路由
268	  step 顶部排空 rx → pending_control                  │ client.load(req).await
269	  批空闲时应用命令 → oneshot 应答 ◀───────────────────┘
270	  （命令改权重前，其后到达的生成请求先缓在
271	   post_control_deferred，防止用错适配器集合）
272	```
273	
274	命令往返（`roundtrip`）的两端都可能失败：`send` 失败说明接收端（调度器线程）已消失；`rx.await` 失败说明引擎收到命令但应答槽被 drop（引擎在应用前拆除了）。两种都折叠为 `LoraControlError::EngineGone`。

338	### 4.3 LoRA 路由层：管理路由与 OpenAI 代理路由
339	
340	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
341	
342	LoRA 服务面在 HTTP 上呈现两组路由，都定义在 lora.rs：
343	
344	- **管理路由** `/v1/load_lora_adapter`、`/v1/unload_lora_adapter`：vLLM 风格的适配器装卸接口，handler 做参数校验后直通 `LoraClient`，是控制通道的 HTTP 门户。
345	- **OpenAI 代理路由** `/v1/models`、`/v1/completions`、`/v1/chat/completions`：让客户端**用适配器名当 `model` 字段**来点名适配器。代理路由把 `model` 改写回基座名、把适配器名注入 `vllm_xargs` 侧信道，再转交给真正的 vLLM 路由。
346	
347	「适配器名当 model 名」是 vLLM 生态的惯例：客户端不需要新 API，`model: "my-adapter"` 就选用了 `my-adapter`。`/v1/models` 则把基座名与已装载适配器名合并列出，客户端能发现可用适配器。两组路由共享一个 `Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>`（已装载适配器名集合），管理路由装卸时更新它，代理路由改写时查它。
348	
349	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
350	
351	**管理路由**（以 load 为例）：
352	
353	```
354	POST /v1/load_lora_adapter {lora_name, lora_path, load_inplace?, is_3d_lora_weight?}
355	  → 本地校验：name 非空 / path 非空 / is_3d_lora_weight 必须为 false（否则 400）
356	  → control.load(LoadLoraAdapterRequest).await
357	      Ok        → adapter_names.insert(name) → 200 "Success: ... added successfully."
358	      EngineGone→ 503 {"error": "engine is gone"}
359	      Failed(m) → 400 {"error": m}
360	```

414	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
415	
416	**练习 1**：为什么代理路由对「未知 model 名」原样放行，而不是自己报 404？
417	
418	**答案**：改写层的职责边界是「把已装载适配器名翻译回基座名」。未知名字可能是拼错的适配器，也可能是任何 vLLM 上游认识的别名——上游对未知 model 自有错误处理（model not found），由它回答语义最准确；改写层自作主张报 404 反而可能拦下上游本可服务的请求。同理，没有 `model` 字段的请求（对 `/v1/completions` 而言 model 本就可选）直接放行。
419	
420	**练习 2**：`adapter_names` 为什么用 `RwLock<HashSet>` 而不是普通 `Mutex<Vec>`？
421	
422	**答案**：读写两种负载不同：管理路由低频写，代理路由**每个生成请求**都要查一次成员资格。`RwLock` 让高频读互不阻塞（且读侧用 `.read().await`，在 tokio 的异步锁上不占 worker 线程）；`HashSet` 把成员判断做成 O(1)。`Vec` + `Mutex` 会让所有请求在改写时排队。另外 `Arc` 共享让管理路由、代理路由、models 路由看到同一个集合——它就是「当前装载了什么」的唯一真相。
423	
424	**练习 3**：启动装载失败与运行期 `/v1/load_lora_adapter` 失败，待遇为何不同？
425	
426	**答案**：启动装载失败以 `?` 中止整个启动（错误带模块名与路径上下文）——`--lora-modules` 是运维显式声明的期望状态，缺一块就不该带病上线；运行期装卸是客户端发起的动态操作，失败映射为可重试的 400/503 响应，服务继续运行。这与 u4-l1 「引擎计数对账宁可死不带病服务」是同一条纪律：声明的东西必须齐。

428	### 4.4 装配与触发链：从 `--enable-lora` 到 serve_model_with_lora_routes

430	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
431	
432	u2-l5 讲过 `ServePlan` 的 `lora_modules: Option<Vec<LoraModule>>` 与 `prefill_only: bool` 两个字段——本讲的两个特殊服务面正是被它们点亮的。`main.rs` 依 plan 三分支，而 **LoRA 分支是唯一串行的**：它 `await` 引擎加载完成才调 serve，且只接受 `LaunchedEngine::Stepped`。两个「为什么」：
433	
434	1. **为何串行**：LoRA 路由的构造闭包需要**捕获引擎的控制平面**（`LoraClient`），而客户端在 `Engine` 交接包里——引擎没加载完，闭包的原料就不存在。对比默认分支：它传给 serve 的是一个引擎 `Future`，HTTP 前端装配（秒级）与权重加载（分钟级）并发（u4-l1）。
435	2. **为何只认 Stepped**：`lora: Option<LoraClient>` 字段长在 `Engine`（step 契约的交接包）上，legacy `EngineHandle` 没有这个字段。LoRA 服务面从一开始就是 step 契约的能力，不为 legacy 契约补造。

# 特殊服务面：prefill-only 门与 LoRA 路由

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 走查 prefill-only 校验门的完整执行路径：读 body → 解析 JSON → 判定 `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` 恰为 1 → 重写 Content-Length → 转发内层路由，否则返回 400。
2. 解释 `Engine::lora` 上的 `Option<LoraClient>` 为什么就是「这个引擎能管理 LoRA 适配器」这一能力本身，以及为什么未铸造控制通道的引擎连「unsupported」错误都不会有。
3. 复述 `--enable-lora` 从 CLI flag 一路到 `serve_model_with_lora_routes` 的完整触发链，并说清 main.rs 的 LoRA 分支为何必须串行等待引擎、为何只接受 `LaunchedEngine::Stepped`。
4. 自己动手用 `tower::ServiceExt::oneshot` 驱动一个挂了 prefill-only 门的 axum Router，观察 400 与透传两种结局。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 回顾：路由扩展链的最里层

在 u4-l2 我们看过装配骨架把最终路由包成三层洋葱：

```
normalize_chat_requests( mark_history( extend_router(router) ) )
        最外：effort 别名改写    内：边界测量      最里：形态选择
```

`extend_router` 有三种形态：默认服务是恒等函数（`|router| router`）；本讲的两个「特殊服务面」正是另外两种——prefill-only 门（`request_contract::prefill_only_routes`）与 LoRA 路由合并（一个 merge + fallback 闭包）。也就是说，**「这台服务器以什么契约对外服务」这个决定，落点就在 `extend_router` 这一层的函数选择上**，而选择权在 `ServePlan`（u2-l5）手里。

### 2.2 P/D 分离与 prefill-only 角色

u2-l5 提过 `ServePlan::prefill_only` 字段。在 P/D（prefill/decode 分离）部署里，一个实例可以只扮演 prefill 角色：它只计算 prompt 的 KV 缓存并保存/导出，不做自回归生成。在 OpenAI 协议上，「只 prefill、不生成」被表达为 `max_tokens=1`——算完 prompt 后产出恰好一个 token 就停。`prefill_only` 置位的实例（如 GLM5.2 TP4 P/D prefill 角色）必须拒绝一切别的请求形状，否则上游会误以为它在正常生成。这个「拒绝」不是引擎内部的调度器规则，而是**在 HTTP 路由层、请求触达引擎之前**就完成的协议契约检查。

### 2.3 LoRA 是什么

LoRA（Low-Rank Adaptation）是一种轻量的模型微调方法：冻结基座权重，只为若干线性层附加一对低秩矩阵 \( A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d} \)、\( B \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r} \)（秩 \( r \ll d \)），推理时叠加 \( BA \) 的输出。一个「适配器（adapter）」就是一组这样的小矩阵，体积远小于基座。服务侧的价值：一个基座可以同时驻留多个适配器，每个请求点名用哪一个——比每个微调副本都载入一份基座便宜得多。

本讲关心的是服务面：适配器如何动态装卸（管理路由）、请求如何点名适配器（`model` 字段）、控制命令如何到达引擎（控制通道）。

### 2.4 axum/tower 速成：Router、fallback_service 与 oneshot

- **axum `Router`** 是一个路由表 + 回调的服务类型；`Router::new().route("/path", post(handler))` 注册路径。
- **`fallback_service(inner)`**：给外层 Router 装一个「兜底服务」——凡是没有命中已注册路径的请求，整包转交给 `inner`。本讲两个特殊路由都用它把「自己管的路径」和「其余一切」分开。
- **`tower::ServiceExt::oneshot(request)`**：不经过网络，直接把一个构造好的 `Request` 喂给服务并拿到 `Response`，是 axum 生态里测试中间层/路由的标准手法（项目测试大量使用）。
- **缓冲改写模式**：中间层要用 `axum::body::to_bytes(body, limit)` 把流式 body 读成完整字节，检查/改写后重新构造 `Body::from(bytes)`，并**重写 `Content-Length` 头**——原始头描述的是进来的流（可能根本没有该头），重建的 body 需要一个准确的头。u4-l2 的 effort 改写、本讲的 prefill 门与 LoRA 转发器共用这个模式。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|------|------|
| `pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs` | prefill-only 校验门：两条 OpenAI 生成路由上的 `max_tokens=1` 强制检查 |
| `pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs` | LoRA 控制通道的词汇表：`LoraControl` 命令、`LoraClient` 异步客户端、`LoraControlError` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 prefill-only 校验门

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

prefill-only 实例对外的协议契约是「每个生成请求必须 `max_tokens=1`」。这个契约若靠引擎内部检查，错误要等请求穿过 HTTP 层、引擎桥、调度器之后才暴露，且错误形态是引擎的内部错误而非 HTTP 语义。所以它被实现为一个 **axum 层的校验中间层**：请求在进入 vLLM 路由（更别说引擎）之前，先被拦下检查 body，不合格立即返回 400 与 OpenAI 风格的错误 JSON。这带来三个好处：

1. 错误以 HTTP 状态码和 `invalid_request_error` 类型表达，上游 SDK 能直接理解；
2. 引擎永远不会收到违反其角色的请求，调度器无需为此设分支；
3. 检查逻辑集中在一个 ~90 行的文件里，可独立用 `oneshot` 测试。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
POST /v1/completions 或 /v1/chat/completions
        │
        ▼
┌─ validate_prefill_only ──────────────────────────┐
│ 1. to_bytes 缓冲 body（上限 16 MiB）             │
│ 2. serde_json 解析为 Value                        │
│ 3. 取 max_tokens、max_completion_tokens（as_u64） │
│ 4. chat 路径：两者都给 → 必须相等，否则 400        │
│ 5. effective = chat ? max_completion_tokens       │
│                .or(max_tokens) : max_tokens       │
│ 6. effective 必须是 Some(1)，否则 400             │
│ 7. 重写 Content-Length = body.len()               │
│ 8. vllm_router.oneshot(重建的请求) 透传           │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
其余路径（/v1/models、/health 等）→ fallback_service 直接进内层路由，不检查
```

判定表（`T` = 该字段的 u64 值，`—` = 缺失或非 u64）：

| 路径 | max_tokens | max_completion_tokens | effective | 结果 |
|------|-----------|----------------------|-----------|------|
| `/v1/completions` | 1 | 任意（不看） | 1 | 透传 |
| `/v1/completions` | 2 或 `—` | 任意 | 2 或 None | 400 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 透传 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 1 | 2 | —（先报冲突） | 400（conflicts） |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | `—` | 1 | 1 | 透传 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | `—` | `—` | None | 400（omitted） |

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**外层路由与兜底。** 门构造一个新的 Router，只注册两条 OpenAI 生成路径，其余一切交给 `fallback_service` 原样放行——所以 prefill-only 实例的 `/v1/models` 等非生成路由行为与默认服务完全一致：[request_contract.rs:L16-L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L16-L22)。注意 `.with_state(vllm_router.clone())` 把内层 Router 当作 handler 的 state 传入，闭包里再 clone 一次作为 fallback。

**错误形态。** 任何检查失败都折叠成一个 400 响应，body 是 OpenAI 风格的错误信封，`message` 用 `anyhow` 的 `{error:#}` 展开完整因果链：[request_contract.rs:L24-L42](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L24-L42)。`type` 与 `code` 都是 `invalid_request_error`——与 vLLM 上游对非法请求的分类一致，上游 SDK 的错误分支能直接命中。

**核心判定。** 缓冲与解析（16 MiB 上限 `REQUEST_BODY_LIMIT` 在 [L14](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L14)）：[request_contract.rs:L48-L53](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L48-L53)。两个 token 上限字段用 `as_u64` 提取——字符串、浮点、负数都会得到 `None`，等价于「缺失」，最终落入 `omitted` 的 400 分支，这就是格式错误也在门前被拦截的原因。chat 路径的同给冲突检查与 effective 折算：[request_contract.rs:L58-L72](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L58-L72)——`/v1/completions` 只认 `max_tokens`，OpenAI 的老接口本来就没有 `max_completion_tokens`，给了也不看（给了 1 仍然 400，见判定表第 2 行，这是有测试锁定的刻意行为）。契约本体只有一条 `ensure!`：[request_contract.rs:L73-L77](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L73-L77)，错误消息把实际收到的值（或 `omitted`）拼进去，用户不需要猜哪里错。

**重写头并透传。** 通过检查的请求在这里重建：[request_contract.rs:L78-L86](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L78-L86)。门本身不改 body 字节（长度其实没变），但请求可能是以 chunked 编码到来的（此时根本没有 `Content-Length` 头），而 `parts.headers` 是原样继承的——从缓冲字节重建 body 就必须重设一个准确的头。`oneshot` 把请求整包交给内层 vLLM Router，它的响应原样返回给客户端。

**serve 侧的接线。** prefill 分支最终把 `prefill_only_routes` 作为 `extend_router` 传入骨架：[vllm/mod.rs:L158-L182](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/mod.rs#L158-L182)，函数文档写明「引擎在此拒绝它不服务的东西，请求到达引擎之前先 400」。骨架最终把它包进 `mark_history` 与 `normalize_chat_requests` 之内：[vllm/mod.rs:L493-L500](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/mod.rs#L493-L500)。也就是说一个 prefill 请求的实际旅程是：effort 别名改写 → 会话边界测量 → **prefill 门** → vLLM 路由 → 引擎桥。

**现成的行为锁定测试。** 两个测试分别锁接受案与驳案：[request_contract.rs:L100-L115](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L100-L115) 断言 chat 路径三种 `=1` 的写法都透传到内层（内层是个返回 200 的假 Router）；[request_contract.rs:L117-L136](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L117-L136) 断言 `max_tokens=2`、两字段冲突、`/v1/completions` 只给 `max_completion_tokens` 三种形状都 400。这两个测试就是判定表的机器可读版本。

   ```rust
   use axum::Json;
   use axum::Router;
   use axum::body::Body;
   use axum::body::to_bytes;
   use axum::extract::Request;
   use axum::http::StatusCode;
   use axum::response::IntoResponse;
   use axum::response::Response;
   use axum::routing::post;
   use serde_json::json;
   use tower::ServiceExt as _;

   pub fn prefill_gate(inner: Router) -> Router {
       Router::new()
           .route("/v1/completions", post(validate))
           .with_state(inner.clone())
           .fallback_service(inner)
   }

   async fn validate(
       axum::extract::State(inner): axum::extract::State<Router>,
       request: Request,
   ) -> Response {
       let (mut parts, body) = request.into_parts();
       let body = to_bytes(body, 16 * 1024 * 1024).await.expect("body");
       let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&body).expect("json");
       let max_tokens = value.get("max_tokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64());
       if max_tokens != Some(1) {
           return (
               StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
               Json(json!({
                   "error": {
                       "message": format!("prefill only routes require max_tokens=1, got {}",
                           max_tokens.map_or("omitted".to_owned(), |v| v.to_string())),
                       "type": "invalid_request_error",
                       "code": "invalid_request_error"
                   }
               })),
           ).into_response();
       }
       parts.headers.insert(
           axum::http::header::CONTENT_LENGTH,
           axum::http::HeaderValue::from_str(&body.len().to_string()).unwrap(),
       );
       inner.oneshot(Request::from_parts(parts, Body::from(body)))
           .await
           .expect("inner router")
   }

   #[cfg(test)]

       use axum::http::StatusCode;
       use axum::routing::any;

           // 正好观察「透传到内层 fallback」。
           let inner = Router::new().fallback(|| async { "inner-fallback" });
           let gate = prefill_gate(inner);

               .body(Body::from(r#"{"max_tokens":2}"#)).unwrap();

           assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
           let bytes = to_bytes(resp.into_body(), usize::MAX).await.unwrap();
           let err: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
           assert_eq!(err["error"]["type"], "invalid_request_error");

           // max_tokens=1 → 透传到内层 fallback
           let req = Request::post("/v1/completions")
               .body(Body::from(r#"{"max_tokens":1}"#)).unwrap();
           let resp = gate.oneshot(req).await.unwrap();
           assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::OK);

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：对 `/v1/completions` 发 `{"max_completion_tokens": 1}`（不带 `max_tokens`）会怎样？为什么这条规则和 `/v1/chat/completions` 不同？

**答案**：400，`effective_max_tokens` 是 `None`（`/v1/completions` 分支只读 `max_tokens`），错误消息为 `... got omitted`。差异的原因是协议本身：`/v1/completions`（旧版补全接口）只有 `max_tokens` 字段，`max_completion_tokens` 是 chat 接口的新拼写，所以在 completions 路径上它不是合法的替身。这条行为由测试 `("/v1/completions", r#"{"max_completion_tokens":1}"#) → BAD_REQUEST` 显式锁定。

**练习 2**：门为什么要把 `/v1/models`、`/health` 这类路径放行？如果门不放行会发生什么？

**答案**：门的契约只约束「生成请求」——prefill-only 角色的限制是「不做自回归生成」，不是「不服务任何 HTTP」。路由发现、健康检查、模型列表与普通实例行为一致，上游才能用同一套客户端管理它。若不放行（例如把检查挂成全局 middleware），这些路径要么 404 要么 400，实例在集群里看起来像坏了。实现上就是 `fallback_service(vllm_router)` 一行。

**练习 3**：请求以 `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` 到达（没有 `Content-Length`），门转发时为什么必须手工重写该头？

**答案**：门用 `to_bytes` 把流式 body 缓冲成完整字节再重建 `Body::from(body)`。原始 `parts.headers` 里要么没有 `Content-Length`（chunked），要么描述的是已被消费的流；重建后的 body 是一个已知长度的整体，下游若按头读定长会出错。所以转发前用 `body.len()` 重设（[request_contract.rs:L78-L82](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/request_contract.rs#L78-L82)）。

### 4.2 LoRA 控制通道：LoraClient 是能力本身

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

u3-l5 讲过 `Scheduler` trait 只有三个方法——`submit`、`step`、`metrics`——并且「超出三方法的能力由调度器自建通道、在自己的 step 里排空」。LoRA 适配器的动态装卸就是这句话的实例：装载/卸载适配器会改变引擎的权重状态，必须由调度器在安全时机（批空闲时）应用，因此它不适合塞进 `Scheduler` 契约，而是**一条独立的控制通道**。

这条通道的设计核心是一个类型层面的决定：引擎交接包 `Engine` 上挂着 `lora: Option<LoraClient>`。**这个 `Option` 就是能力本身**——`Some` 表示「这个引擎能管理适配器，拿着客户端就能下命令」；`None` 表示「这个引擎没有这门能力」。注意这里**不存在「unsupported」错误路径**：没有铸造通道的引擎压根不会挂载 LoRA 路由，无人能「问」它，也就无需回答。对比一下常见的替代设计（布尔开关 `supports_lora` + 调用时返回 `Unsupported` 错误）：开关与客户端可能不一致（开关开着但客户端忘了给），而 `Option` 里要么有可用的客户端、要么没有，第二种真相源不存在。lora.rs 测试里的一条注释把这一点说得很直白：「An engine without LoRA never mounts these routes at all — the `Option` on `Engine::lora` is the capability」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
引擎侧（模型 crate，以 qwen3 为例）                    服务侧（frontend）
─────────────────────────                            ─────────────────────
launch 时：
  LoraClient::channel() ──铸出──▶ (client, rx)
  rx 交给调度器（spawn 前捕获）
  Engine { lora: Some(client), .. } ──────────────▶ serve_model_with_lora_routes
                                                      │ 取出 client（None → 显式报错）
                                                      ▼
调度器每一步：                                    /v1/load_lora_adapter 路由
  step 顶部排空 rx → pending_control                  │ client.load(req).await
  批空闲时应用命令 → oneshot 应答 ◀───────────────────┘
  （命令改权重前，其后到达的生成请求先缓在
   post_control_deferred，防止用错适配器集合）
```

命令往返（`roundtrip`）的两端都可能失败：`send` 失败说明接收端（调度器线程）已消失；`rx.await` 失败说明引擎收到命令但应答槽被 drop（引擎在应用前拆除了）。两种都折叠为 `LoraControlError::EngineGone`。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**模块文档——设计意图的第一手陈述**：[control.rs:L1-L11](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs#L1-L11)。三句话概括：通道由引擎自己铸造；接收端在 `step` 内排空、批空闲时应用；词汇表（命令类型）定义在 frontend 层——**客户端的使用者定义词汇**——使 frontend 不依赖任何模型 crate 类型。

**命令词汇**：[control.rs:L30-L45](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs#L30-L45)。`LoraControl` 三个变体 `Load`/`Unload`/`List`，每个都自带一个 `oneshot::Sender` 应答槽——命令与「往哪儿回话」是一个值，不存在关联 id 的簿记。接收端类型是 `crossbeam_channel::Receiver<LoraControl>`：[control.rs:L47-L49](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs#L47-L49)——选 crossbeam 而非 tokio mpsc，因为消费者是调度器线程里的同步代码（与 u3-l6 里「提交通道选 crossbeam」同理）。

**客户端与铸造**：[control.rs:L60-L73](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs#L60-L73)。`LoraClient` 只是 `crossbeam Sender` 的包装，`Clone` 成本是一次通道引用计数；`channel()` 一行铸造双端。三个异步方法 `load`/`unload`/`list` 全部委托给同一个 `roundtrip`：[control.rs:L75-L103](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/control.rs#L75-L103)——`send` 与 `await` 各映射到 `EngineGone`，引擎侧的 `Err(String)` 映射到 `Failed`。客户端是异步的（HTTP handler 直接 `.await`），但传输是同步队列：命令瞬时入队，等待只发生在应答槽上。

### 4.3 LoRA 路由层：管理路由与 OpenAI 代理路由

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

LoRA 服务面在 HTTP 上呈现两组路由，都定义在 lora.rs：

- **管理路由** `/v1/load_lora_adapter`、`/v1/unload_lora_adapter`：vLLM 风格的适配器装卸接口，handler 做参数校验后直通 `LoraClient`，是控制通道的 HTTP 门户。
- **OpenAI 代理路由** `/v1/models`、`/v1/completions`、`/v1/chat/completions`：让客户端**用适配器名当 `model` 字段**来点名适配器。代理路由把 `model` 改写回基座名、把适配器名注入 `vllm_xargs` 侧信道，再转交给真正的 vLLM 路由。

「适配器名当 model 名」是 vLLM 生态的惯例：客户端不需要新 API，`model: "my-adapter"` 就选用了 `my-adapter`。`/v1/models` 则把基座名与已装载适配器名合并列出，客户端能发现可用适配器。两组路由共享一个 `Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>`（已装载适配器名集合），管理路由装卸时更新它，代理路由改写时查它。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

**管理路由**（以 load 为例）：

```
POST /v1/load_lora_adapter {lora_name, lora_path, load_inplace?, is_3d_lora_weight?}
  → 本地校验：name 非空 / path 非空 / is_3d_lora_weight 必须为 false（否则 400）
  → control.load(LoadLoraAdapterRequest).await
      Ok        → adapter_names.insert(name) → 200 "Success: ... added successfully."
      EngineGone→ 503 {"error": "engine is gone"}
      Failed(m) → 400 {"error": m}
```

**OpenAI 代理改写决策树**（`rewrite_lora_request_body`）：

```
读 body JSON
  ├─ 没有 "model" 字符串字段 ──────────────▶ 原样放行（交给 vLLM 自己报错）
  ├─ model == base_model_name ────────────▶ 原样放行（基座请求，无需改写）
  ├─ model ∉ adapter_names（读锁查集合）──▶ 原样放行（未知名字留给上游判 404）
  └─ model ∈ adapter_names ───────────────▶ 改写：
        model ← base_model_name
        vllm_xargs["pegainfer_lora_adapter"] ← 适配器名（保留 xargs 里已有的键）
        重新序列化 body → 重写 Content-Length → oneshot 进 vLLM 路由
```

改写注入的 `vllm_xargs` 键随后开始它的**侧信道旅程**：vLLM 上游把它放进 `sampling_params.extra_args` 原样下传；stepped 桥用 `lora_adapter_from_sampling_params` 提取（空串/非字符串直接拒绝该请求）并写进 `Request::lora_adapter` 字段，随提交进入调度器——调度器据此为该请求选适配器。整条链上「适配器选择」从不占用 OpenAI 协议的正式字段，全部走 `vllm_xargs`。

**练习 1**：为什么代理路由对「未知 model 名」原样放行，而不是自己报 404？

**答案**：改写层的职责边界是「把已装载适配器名翻译回基座名」。未知名字可能是拼错的适配器，也可能是任何 vLLM 上游认识的别名——上游对未知 model 自有错误处理（model not found），由它回答语义最准确；改写层自作主张报 404 反而可能拦下上游本可服务的请求。同理，没有 `model` 字段的请求（对 `/v1/completions` 而言 model 本就可选）直接放行。

**练习 2**：`adapter_names` 为什么用 `RwLock<HashSet>` 而不是普通 `Mutex<Vec>`？

**答案**：读写两种负载不同：管理路由低频写，代理路由**每个生成请求**都要查一次成员资格。`RwLock` 让高频读互不阻塞（且读侧用 `.read().await`，在 tokio 的异步锁上不占 worker 线程）；`HashSet` 把成员判断做成 O(1)。`Vec` + `Mutex` 会让所有请求在改写时排队。另外 `Arc` 共享让管理路由、代理路由、models 路由看到同一个集合——它就是「当前装载了什么」的唯一真相。

**练习 3**：启动装载失败与运行期 `/v1/load_lora_adapter` 失败，待遇为何不同？

**答案**：启动装载失败以 `?` 中止整个启动（错误带模块名与路径上下文）——`--lora-modules` 是运维显式声明的期望状态，缺一块就不该带病上线；运行期装卸是客户端发起的动态操作，失败映射为可重试的 400/503 响应，服务继续运行。这与 u4-l1 「引擎计数对账宁可死不带病服务」是同一条纪律：声明的东西必须齐。

### 4.4 装配与触发链：从 `--enable-lora` 到 serve_model_with_lora_routes

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

u2-l5 讲过 `ServePlan` 的 `lora_modules: Option<Vec<LoraModule>>` 与 `prefill_only: bool` 两个字段——本讲的两个特殊服务面正是被它们点亮的。`main.rs` 依 plan 三分支，而 **LoRA 分支是唯一串行的**：它 `await` 引擎加载完成才调 serve，且只接受 `LaunchedEngine::Stepped`。两个「为什么」：

1. **为何串行**：LoRA 路由的构造闭包需要**捕获引擎的控制平面**（`LoraClient`），而客户端在 `Engine` 交接包里——引擎没加载完，闭包的原料就不存在。对比默认分支：它传给 serve 的是一个引擎 `Future`，HTTP 前端装配（秒级）与权重加载（分钟级）并发（u4-l1）。
2. **为何只认 Stepped**：`lora: Option<LoraClient>` 字段长在 `Engine`（step 契约的交接包）上，legacy `EngineHandle` 没有这个字段。LoRA 服务面从一开始就是 step 契约的能力，不为 legacy 契约补造。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

`--enable-lora` 的完整触发链（十四步）：

```

## 6. 本讲小结

- **prefill-only 门**是 axum 层的协议契约检查：缓冲 body → 判 `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` 恰为 1（completions 只认前者，chat 两者同给须相等）→ 重写 Content-Length 后 `oneshot` 透传；不合格在触达引擎之前得到 400 + `invalid_request_error` 信封。非生成路径经 `fallback_service` 原样放行。
- **LoRA 能力的类型化**：`Engine::lora: Option<LoraClient>` 上的 `Option` 就是能力本身——没有通道的引擎不挂 LoRA 路由，无人能问，因此错误枚举里没有 `Unsupported`；唯一显式的错误在装配侧（引擎与 `--enable-lora` 说法不一致时拒绝启动）。
- **控制通道**：引擎 launch 时 `LoraClient::channel()` 铸双端，接收端随调度器走、在 `step` 顶部排空、批空闲时应用；命令走 crossbeam、应答走 tokio oneshot，两端消失都折叠为 `EngineGone`。
- **LoRA 路由两组**：管理路由（load/unload，直通控制通道，成功 200 文本、EngineGone 503、Failed 400）与 OpenAI 代理路由（`model` = 适配器名 → 改回基座名 + 注入 `vllm_xargs.pegainfer_lora_adapter`，经桥提取为 `Request::lora_adapter`；`/v1/models` 合并基座与适配器名排序去重列出）。
- **触发链与串行原因**：`--enable-lora` → validate 从属/互斥规则 → `serve_plan.lora_modules=Some(...)` → main LoRA 分支；串行是因为路由闭包要捕获引擎控制平面、且 `lora` 字段只在 step 契约的 `Engine` 上，故必须 await 加载并要求 `LaunchedEngine::Stepped`，`engine_count` 随之硬编码 1。
- **洋葱位置**：两个特殊路由都是 `extend_router` 的形态（最里层），外层依次是 `mark_history`、`normalize_chat_requests`——LoRA 改写必须 `or_insert_with` 追加 xargs 以保留边界测量结果，顺序即依赖。

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

    ))
  )
